title: have to / don't have to for Rules and Obligations
grammarTitle: have to / don't have to — Obligation and Lack of Obligation
grammarNote: HAVE TO выражает внешнюю обязанность или необходимость — что-то, требуемое правилами, ситуацией или другими людьми. DON'T HAVE TO означает, что что-то НЕ обязательно — можно не делать, но можно и делать. Важно: don't have to ≠ must not. "Don't have to" = не обязательно. "Must not" = запрещено.

grammarExtra.title: have to vs must — key difference

rows.example: "I must study." = I feel I need to (personal decision). No external rule.
"I have to submit this by Friday." = the university requires it. External rule.
"You must eat well." ≈ "You have to eat well." — both common for obligation.
"I had to wait." ✅ "I must wait." (no past form!) → use "had to" for past obligation.

grammarExtra.title: don't have to vs must not

rows.example: "You don't have to take vitamins." = Optional — no obligation. You can if you want.
"You must not smoke in the hospital." = Forbidden! It's a rule/law.
"You don't have to wear a uniform." ≠ "You must not wear a uniform." — very different!

rows.form: He/She = has to / doesn't have to
rows.example: "She HAS TO submit." / "She DOESN'T HAVE TO submit." ✅
"I have to go to the clinic today." / "She has to rest."

rows.form: Past: had to / didn't have to
rows.example: "He had to wait two hours." / "We didn't have to pay." ✅
"You will have to retake the exam if you fail." ✅
"Do you have to submit it today?" / "Did she have to redo it?" ✅
✅ "She HAS TO go." — he/she/it → HAS TO (not "have to")!

rows.form: ✗ "I don't have to go there." (as if forbidden)
rows.example: ✅ "I don't have to go there." = I'm NOT OBLIGED to. NOT "it's forbidden."
✅ "He HAD TO go yesterday." — past of obligation = "had to", never "musted"!
✅ "Do you HAVE TO go?" — to form questions, use "have to". "Must" has no question with "do".

grammarTip:
HAVE TO / DON'T HAVE TO — обязанность:

have to + base form = ОБЯЗАН (внешнее требование):
"I have to submit by Friday." (дедлайн)
"She has to see a doctor." (she/he → HAS to!)

don't have to = НЕ ОБЯЗАН (необязательно):
"You don't have to take vitamins." (можно, но необязательно)
"He doesn't have to come." (he/she → DOESN'T have to)

⚠️ Критическая разница:
don't have to = не обязательно (можешь делать или нет)
must not = ЗАПРЕЩЕНО!

Прошедшее: had to / didn't have to
"She had to wait." ✅
"She didn't have to pay." ✅
✗ Никогда не говори: "She musted wait."

exercises.text: She ___ submit her essay by Thursday — it's a strict deadline.
exercises.hint: "she" → HAS TO. "She HAS TO submit by Thursday." ✅ (he/she/it = has to)

exercises.instruction: Choose: don't have to or must not?
exercises.text: "You ___ wear a uniform at WKU." (it's not required, but not forbidden)
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = not obligatory. "You DON'T HAVE TO wear a uniform." ✅

exercises.text: "He ___ (go) to the clinic yesterday — his appointment was cancelled."
exercises.hint: Past negative: "He DIDN'T HAVE TO GO." = it was not necessary. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose: don't have to or must not?
exercises.text: "You ___ smoke in this building." (it's strictly forbidden)
exercises.hint: "must not" = forbidden. "You MUST NOT smoke in this building." ✅ (Not "don't have to" — that would mean it's optional)

exercises.text: "I ___ wait three hours at the clinic last week."
exercises.hint: Past obligation: "I HAD TO WAIT three hours." ✅ Never "musted" — it doesn't exist!

exercises.instruction: Complete with have to, has to, or don't have to.
exercises.text: "You ___ take intense exercise. Even walking helps."
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = not necessary. "You DON'T HAVE TO take intense exercise." ✅

exercises.text: "___ you see the doctor today?" (is it necessary?)
exercises.hint: Questions with "have to": DO/DOES + subject + have to + base. "DO YOU HAVE TO see...?" ✅

exercises.text: "She have to rest more." — Is this correct?
opts: No — should be "She has to rest more."
No — should be "She must to rest."
No — should be "She should to rest."
exercises.correct: No — should be "She has to rest more."
exercises.hint: "she" → HAS TO (not "have to"). "She HAS TO rest more." ✅

exercises.text: "If your symptoms don't improve, you ___ come back."
exercises.hint: Future obligation: "will have to + base". "You WILL HAVE TO come back." ✅

exercises.text: "I have to take a blood test." → Yesterday: "I ___ ."
exercises.correct: had to take a blood test
exercises.hint: Past of "have to" = "HAD TO". "I HAD TO TAKE a blood test yesterday." ✅

exercises.text: "You don't have to come to the meeting." means:
opts: It's not necessary — you can choose
exercises.correct: It's not necessary — you can choose
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = not obligatory. You can come or not. ✅
✗ "musted" — NEVER correct. ✅ "He HAD TO wait." — past obligation = "had to". ✅

questions.hint: "have to" = obligation required by rules, others, or a situation. External. ✅
"she" → HAS TO (not "have to"). "She HAS TO see the doctor." ✅
"don't have to" = not obligatory. You can do it or not. ✅

questions.text: "You must not smoke here." vs "You don't have to smoke here." — Difference:
opts: "must not" = forbidden; "don't have to" = not necessary
questions.correct: "must not" = forbidden; "don't have to" = not necessary
questions.hint: Critical difference: "must not" = prohibited. "don't have to" = optional, not obligatory. ✅

questions.text: "I ___ wait two hours at the clinic yesterday." (past obligation)
questions.hint: Past of "have to" = "HAD TO". "I HAD TO WAIT two hours yesterday." ✅
✅ "He HAD TO go." — there is no "musted". Past obligation = always "had to". ✅

questions.text: Form a question: "Is it necessary to submit today?"
questions.hint: "Do/Does + subject + have to + base?" ✅ "DO YOU HAVE TO submit today?"

opts: Paying was not necessary — we had a choice
questions.correct: Paying was not necessary — we had a choice
questions.hint: "didn't have to" = past: not obligatory. We could choose. ✅

questions.text: "If things don't improve, you ___ come back." (future obligation)
questions.hint: Future: "will have to + base". "You WILL HAVE TO come back." ✅

questions.text: "I must finish this essay." vs "I have to finish this essay." — Difference:
opts: Must = personal feeling of obligation; have to = external requirement
questions.correct: Must = personal feeling of obligation; have to = external requirement
questions.hint: "must" = internal pressure. "have to" = external rule or deadline. Often interchangeable in practice. ✅

questions.text: "Do I have to wear a uniform?" The answer "No, you don't." means:
questions.hint: "No, you don't have to." = Not necessary. You can choose whether to wear one. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ rewrite her essay. The professor rejected it." (past obligation)
questions.hint: "had to" = past obligation. "She HAD TO REWRITE her essay." ✅

questions.text: "You don't have to take vitamins." — Correct interpretation:
opts: Taking vitamins is optional — not required
questions.correct: Taking vitamins is optional — not required
questions.hint: "don't have to" = not obligatory. Taking vitamins is optional. ✅

questions.text: Past form of "I have to go" is:
questions.hint: Past of "have to" = "HAD TO". "I HAD TO GO." ✅

questions.text: "You must not enter." vs "You don't have to enter." — Difference:
questions.hint: Critical! "Must not" = PROHIBITED. "Don't have to" = NOT NECESSARY. ✅
